text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Justice ministry, police and private sector come to an agreement on combating white collar fraud. (p1)
- Financial services group ING is to increase its stake in Belgium's Bank Brussel Lambert. (p1)
- Chemicals concern DSM says it has no plans for a new ethylene cracker in the Port of Rotterdam. (p1)
- Claim of 173 million guilders from a group of seven utility companies forces automation firm Multihouse to institute insolvency proceedings. (p3)
- Some 300 jobs have to go at Philips household appliances plant in Hoogeveen. (p3)
- Project developer MAB buys back shopping mall La Vie in Utrecht for redevelopment operation. (p3)
- Akzo Nobel subsidiary Organon challenges new-found link between thrombosis and the use of its light contraceptive pill. (p3)
- ING's participation unit Parcom gets 30 pct stake in Germany's car industry supply company Edscha through management buy out. (p17)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Excesses with options in own company can be easily repaired under existing fiscal laws, answer fiscal specialist to P.M. Wim Kok's call for new legislation. (p1)
- Philips finds new ways to reduce costs. (p2)
- Automation company CSS is to publish its notice of introduction today. (p2)
- Cabinet reserves 1.1 bln guilders in its budget for next period to reduce the tax burden. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Richard Krajicek no. 5 on world ranking list after winning Tokyo tennis tournament. (p1)
- Investors confused by P.M. Wim Kok's call for taxation of profits on investments. (p3)
- KLM pilots think of claiming a seat on the supervisory board, if the airline continues to press for lowering their pay. (p13)
- Cooperation between intermediate businesses is becoming essential for surviving, according to Moret Ernst & Young. (p13)
TROUW
- Liberal coalition party VVD against taxation of capital gain. (p1)
- A rapid fixing of exchange rates of countries participating in the Euro is essential, says F. von Dewall of ING. (p6)
- Philips is unexpectedly successful with its portable phones. (p6)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Number of swine fever cases rises to 111 since outbreak discovered in February. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
